documents.title: H&P - Admission, Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
lines: HPI:
79 y/o male with HFrEF (EF 30% by echo last yr), HTN, CKD3, T2DM presents with 5 days progressive dyspnea and leg swelling.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
Dyspnea now at rest. Orthopnea requiring 3 pillows, 2 episodes PND last night. No fever, no cough. Denies chest pain.
Diet: admits to canned soup and deli meat daily. Daughter reports he skips AM pill about twice a week - pt disagrees.
PMH: HFrEF, HTN, CKD stage 3, T2DM on metformin, gout, BPH.
Home meds: furosemide 80 mg BID, carvedilol 12.5 mg BID, sacubitril/valsartan 49-51 mg BID, spironolactone 25 mg daily, metformin 500 mg BID, allopurinol 100 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qHS.
Allergies: sulfa (rash). Lives with wife, 1 flight of stairs, ambulates with cane.
ED course 21:40:
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED.
Exam 23:15:
BP 158/92, HR 96, T 36.8, respiratory rate 28 with accessory muscle use; speaking 3 to 4 words per breath.
Gen: sitting upright, diaphoretic, in distress. JVP ~14 cm, positive hepatojugular reflux.
Lungs: bibasilar crackles to mid fields, no wheeze.
Cardiac: S3 present, PMI displaced, no murmur appreciated.
Abd: soft, mild RUQ fullness, liver edge 2 cm below costal margin.
Ext: 3+ pitting edema to mid thigh bilaterally, cool feet, pulses 1+.
Labs:
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL on arrival (baseline 1.3 mg/dL from clinic 2 months ago). BUN 48, Na 133, K 4.6, HCO3 24.
Hgb 11.8, WBC 8.2, plt 202. Trop 0.04 flat. LFTs: AST 44, ALT 38, alb 3.2.
Assessment/Plan:
Acute on chronic decompensated HFrEF, volume overloaded, with cardiorenal physiology. Congestion despite outpatient diuretic uptitration.
1. Diuresis: furosemide 80 mg IV every 12 hours. Strict I/O, daily standing weights, foley for accurate UOP.
2. Hold sacubitril/valsartan, spironolactone, metformin given renal function. Continue carvedilol.
3. O2 to keep SpO2 >92%, HOB elevated. 2 g Na diet, 1.5 L fluid restriction. BMP q12h. Cardiology consulted.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD3
lines: Admit dx: acute on chronic decompensated HFrEF. Discharge dx: same, improved.
Hospital course:
Admitted HD1 with severe congestion. Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours.
On admission respiratory rate 28 with accessory muscle use; speaking 3 to 4 words per breath; orthopnea requiring 3 pillows.
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%; remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
BNP 1,480 pg/mL on arrival (prior outpatient value 310 pg/mL).
Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL on arrival (baseline 1.3 mg/dL from clinic 2 months ago), 2.4 mg/dL on hospital day 2.
Converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
HD2 18:00 UOP improved to 1,950 mL over subsequent 12 hrs. Net negative 4.1 L for stay; weight down 3.8 kg to 84.2 kg.
HD3 06:00: creatinine 2.2, K 3.7 (repleted 40 mEq PO), Na 135. Weaned to room air 08:10 with SpO2 94% ambulating in hall.
Exam at discharge: JVP ~8 cm, lungs clear to bases, 1+ ankle edema, speaking full sentences, RR 18.
Discharge meds: furosemide 80 mg PO BID, carvedilol 12.5 mg BID, allopurinol 100 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qHS, KCl 20 mEq daily x5 days.
Held at discharge: sacubitril/valsartan, spironolactone, metformin - to be restarted by cardiology pending renal recovery.
Instructions: daily AM weights, call for gain >1 kg/day or 2 kg/week. 2 g Na diet, 1.5 L fluid restriction reviewed with pt and wife.
Follow-up: cardiology clinic in 5 days with BMP; primary care in 2 weeks. Home RN for weight and med review in 48 hrs.
Discharge condition: stable, ambulating with cane, room air. Discharged HD3 14:20 with daughter.
